title: Tech News You Need Today

slides.headline: Tech News You Need Today
slides.subtitle: From X's creator changes to a mysterious $450 laptop.

slides.headline: X is changing how creators get paid
slides.explanation: X is replacing its revenue-sharing program with a new system called Original Content Rewards starting September 8th. If you create content on the platform, you will need to meet new follower and engagement requirements to qualify.

slides.headline: Can AI actually change professional football?
slides.explanation: Tech investors have been eyeing ways to integrate AI into the World Cup, even if current plans have been cancelled. It raises a big question about whether some parts of our culture should remain untouched by automation.

slides.headline: OpenAI brings new talent on board
slides.explanation: OpenAI has officially acquired the presentation startup NextSlide. The team is already moving over to help build out new features for ChatGPT.

slides.headline: The hunt for a cheap, decent laptop
slides.explanation: Finding a reliable laptop for under $500 has historically been nearly impossible due to low-quality hardware. A new $450 device is challenging the market, but it remains to be seen if it can actually deliver on performance.

slides.headline: Why tech giants nickname hacking groups
slides.explanation: Google is updating how it tracks and labels various hacking groups. An expert explains that these codenames are more than just labels, they are essential for organizing the defense against global cyber threats.

caption:
From major platform updates to the changing landscape of cybersecurity, here is what is happening in tech today. We are breaking down the headlines so you can stay informed without the noise. Which of these stories are you most interested in?

title: Global Updates: Paris, Kyiv, and Beyond

slides.headline: Global Updates: Paris, Kyiv, and Beyond
slides.subtitle: Catch up on the five most important stories happening around the world today.

slides.headline: High diving returns to the Seine
slides.explanation: Athletes are jumping from a 20-metre platform in Paris for the European Aquatics Championships. This event serves as a major test for the city's ongoing efforts to clean up the river's water quality.

slides.headline: New shipping talks in the Strait of Hormuz
slides.explanation: Oman says discussions about a new shipping route are showing signs of progress. While both sides are talking, it remains unclear if these negotiations will lead to a full breakthrough.

slides.headline: Russian missile attacks strike near Kyiv
slides.explanation: A child was among three people killed during overnight Russian strikes. The attacks come as President Zelensky warns that Ukraine is running low on missile interceptors.

slides.headline: US pledges $1bn to Colombia
slides.explanation: The US is offering a billion dollars to Colombia on the same day the new president took office. The new leader has promised a tough stance on narco-terrorism in his first official speech.

slides.headline: Medical report on Brandon Clarke
slides.explanation: Los Angeles authorities confirmed that the NBA player's death was caused by the effects of heroin and cocaine. This report provides final clarity on the cause behind his passing.

caption:
